title: From Classical Cad–Cam Systems to CNC Programming: A Teaching Approach
content: This paper presents a teaching approach for understanding CNC programming, starting from the principles used on TRAUB machine tools and in the SuperDraft CAD–CAM system and continuing with applications on EMCO Concept Turn 60 and Concept Mill 55 equipment, using Siemens and FANUC control interfaces. The method follows five stages, from reading the technical drawing and choosing the work origin to programming and verification of the tool path. Two demonstration parts, for turning and milling, are presented together with an assessment sheet for student activities. The paper has a methodological character and does not report experiments with students or machining made on the equipment. The result is a training structure connecting classical CAD–CAM principles with requirements of present CNC programming.
